'''Young Jedi''' is Decipher's 1999 ''Star Wars'' customizable card game based on ''The Phantom Menace''. It is a different game from [[Star Wars CCG]]. Decipher held both licenses; designers, Squadron Members, and the player base overlapped.

The [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] GeoCities site published two Young Jedi lists next to its Classic Star Wars decks. The lists, ''Wizards!'' (Jedi) and ''All Droids All the time!'' (Sith), were both by Gold 31 ([[Alex Alcalde]]). Archived copies: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/jedi1.html jedi1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20011202101302/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/decks/jedi1.html Wayback, 2 December 2001]; [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html sith1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009020148/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html Wayback, 9 October 2026].

== Sets ==
Decipher released eight Young Jedi sets between May 1999 and September 2001: ''Menace of Darth Maul'', ''The Jedi Council'', ''Battle of Naboo'', ''Enhanced Menace of Darth Maul'', ''Duel of the Fates'', ''Enhanced Battle of Naboo'', ''Young Jedi Reflections'' and ''Boonta Eve Podrace''.<ref name="cl">[http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Young Jedi Card Lists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021201080954/http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Organized play ==
The first Young Jedi World Championship was held at DecipherCon 1999, with 32 players advancing from four Friday qualifiers. Decipher wrote that "most have some Star Wars CCG experience". Greg Heisler won, and Matt Reed was runner-up.<ref name="wc99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Young Jedi World Championship], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000124144623/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The 2000 Young Jedi World Championship, won by Ian Vincent, ran at [[DecipherCon 2000]] alongside the SWCCG World Championship.<ref name="dc00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ Internet Archive]</ref>
